findings.title: canManage() for all groups is granted by the VIEW scope
findings.body: GroupPermissionsV2.canManage() (the no-argument variant used by GroupsResource.addTopLevelGroup via requireManage()) evaluates `hasPermission(null, VIEW, MANAGE)`. This means an admin who only has the `view` scope on the `Groups` resource type is allowed to create top-level groups (and anything else gated by canManage()). The scope list should only contain MANAGE, as canManage(GroupModel) correctly does.

findings.title: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission returns resource IDs and evaluates permissions with the wrong key
findings.body: For FGAP v2 the group resource is created with `name` = group id (AdminPermissionsSchema.resolveGroup) and a separate generated resource `id`. Here the code (a) calls `hasPermission(groupResource.getId(), ...)`, but hasPermission looks the resource up with `resourceStore.findByName(server, groupId)`, so it never finds the per-group resource and always falls back to the "all groups" resource; and (b) adds `groupResource.getId()` to the returned set, while callers (UsersResource.searchForUser via session attribute UserModel.GROUPS, and UsersResource.getUsersCount) expect group IDs. Consequently per-group view-members permissions are ignored by this method and, when a result is returned, user searches/counts are filtered by non-existent group IDs. Use `groupResource.getName()` for both the permission lookup and the returned set.

findings.title: Possible NPE when the "Groups" resource-type resource is absent
findings.body: `AdminPermissionsSchema.getResourceTypeResource` returns null if the schema is not supported for the resource server or the resource is not found. The returned value is used immediately in `policyStore.findByResource(server, resource)` and `resource.getScopes()` without a null check, which would throw a NullPointerException (HTTP 500) instead of simply denying access. Add a null guard returning false.

findings.title: Group removal listener will fail with UnsupportedOperationException when FGAP v2 is enabled
findings.body: AdminPermissions.registerListener (registered when ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ is enabled) handles GroupModel.GroupRemovedEvent by calling `management(session, realm).groups().setPermissionsEnabled(group, false)`. With ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 also enabled, `management()` returns MgmtPermissionsV2, whose new `groups()` override returns GroupPermissionsV2, which throws UnsupportedOperationException from setPermissionsEnabled. Deleting any group (and GroupResource#getManagementPermissions / setManagementPermissionsEnabled, which call isPermissionsEnabled/getPermissions) will therefore fail with a 500 when both features are on.

findings.title: getResourceName does not resolve group names for the new Groups resource type
findings.body: Now that GROUPS is part of the schema, policies of resource type `Groups` store the group id as the resource name. getResourceName only special-cases USERS, so for group permissions it falls through to `resource.getDisplayName()`, which is null for these generated resources. The admin console/REST representation will show no (or a raw) name for group permissions. A branch resolving the group (including the "All groups" case for the resource named `Groups`) is needed.

findings.title: Javadoc on requireManageMembers refers to the wrong method
findings.body: The Javadoc of `requireManageMembers(GroupModel)` states it throws ForbiddenException if `canManageMembership(GroupModel)` returns false; it actually checks `canManageMembers(GroupModel)`. This is misleading for implementers of the interface. Also, `getGroupIdsWithViewPermission` is documented as returning a "Stream of IDs" while it returns a Set.
